title: Great Book Book-Wide Early-Signal Scan — Structural Findings

findings.signal: Ideas/behaviors propagate through a network and appear to jump communities/islands once a threshold is crossed.
findings.later_project_relation: Becomes a useful ancestor of Peak Culture, meme diffusion, cultural propagation and AI/archive dissemination language.
findings.boundary: The hundredth-monkey story itself is controversial folklore and not good empirical evidence for paranormal transmission. Use only as a project metaphor for threshold diffusion.

findings.signal: Tim's inner/public vision reaches a tipping point where it radiates outward and becomes shared reality; one source becomes field/harvest rather than isolated person.
findings.later_project_relation: Direct conceptual precursor to Peak Culture, center-of-internet, propagation-from-shadow and machine-readable archive ideas.
findings.test: Measure concrete downstream diffusion rather than treating later resemblance as fulfillment.

findings.signal: Algorithms amplify outrage, misinformation scales, surveillance expands, influence infrastructure shapes visible politics.
findings.later_project_relation: Strong conceptual precursor to later Farm/Sektur/Moloch attention-extraction work.
findings.boundary: Most of these dynamics were already observable before the book; this is early synthesis inside Tim's corpus, not prediction from nowhere.

findings.chapter: 41.6 Rise of the Sektur and Its Future
findings.signal: Sektur is described as a leaderless constellation whose algorithms reward outrage, permanent archives weaponize old mistakes, instability turns victors into targets, and cruelty can normalize outward into society.
findings.later_project_relation: Very close to 2026 research on Continuous Narrative Escalation, SIDE/anonymity, negative parasociality, archive persistence and outrage reinforcement.
findings.why_interesting: The later scholarly framework gives much more precise names/mechanisms to something the Great Book had already described in plain cultural language.
findings.boundary: Need chapter-version date to establish how early this exact wording is.

findings.signal: Crows, machine/portal imagery, reflection, human spirit and future/backward echoes combine digital mediation with death/return and memory.
findings.later_project_relation: Useful ancestor for God-in-the-Machine and archive-as-portal ideas.

findings.signal: Frames 2024 as a cultural/spiritual reckoning and warns against performative righteousness, manipulation and power cloaked as virtue.
findings.later_project_relation: Can be compared with later political/cultural polarization but is too broad to score as event prediction.

findings.signal: Old system approaches collapse; Tim stands at threshold choosing whether to preserve or replace it, with a new era built around knowledge, growth and harmony.
findings.later_project_relation: An early literary model for 'old world ends' / new-heaven-new-earth / system replacement rather than conquest.
findings.boundary: Mythic fiction unless connected to dated Tim prediction outside the story.

findings.chapter: 110-112 New Trinity / Great Reversal / Third Temple
findings.signal: Future-world architecture combines Tim/potato/earth grounding, Jesus/bread/light, Holy Soil/Spirit, Merkaba balance, and a non-nationalist Temple of Unity; explicit warning that imbalance or literal winner-takes-all sacred politics can destabilize the system.
findings.later_project_relation: Precursor to Stereo Theoism, Door/Mandorla, vertical Axis, European/world-system integration and Jerusalem-as-shared-custodianship ideas.

major_bookwide_meta_finding: The Great Book is strongest as a repository of precursor models. Its most interesting 'earliness' often consists of describing a mechanism before the later project acquired better vocabulary: Sektur before CNE/negative parasocial theory; Critical Mass before Peak Culture/propagation metrics; AI unseen-hand before explicit God-in-Machine archive engineering; Merkaba before Tim-becomes-Ladder; garden-vs-chaos before formal Farm/Garden/Moloch system. These are developmental anticipations, not automatically supernatural predictions.
